# Index

24 cases, newest first. Each line: title — kind, from to to; the share of the changed code AI produced, as the source states it (a contrast case, mostly rule-based, says so in its summary); how far the claims can be checked; the author's stake in the tools; the cost the source gives; a one-line summary.

Lessons drawn from the cases, by aspect: [lessons/index.md](lessons/index.md) (152 lessons on 16 pages). Before a migration: [checklist.md](checklist.md).

Moves covered, by the language the code was in before the move: C (Intel), C++ (Bloomberg, Google, Ladybird), Dart (Google), Go (1Password, Mindstone, Ping.gg), Groovy (PagerDuty), Java (Google, PagerDuty, Spotify, Uber), JavaScript (Checkly, Slack), Python (Bloomberg), Ruby (GitLab), Scala (Spotify), SQL (Spotify, Temporal), TypeScript (Airbnb, Christopher Chedeau, GitHub, Lutz Leonhardt, Slack), Zig (Bun). Each case line below gives the move itself (from, to). Only Bun, Checkly, Christopher Chedeau, GitHub, Intel, Ladybird, Ping.gg and Shopify changed the code's language; the others kept it (a framework, test, data, build or structure move). The language-changing cases that name a language move code out of C, C++, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript and Zig only; for the other languages listed they show moves that kept the language. Language not named: Asana, Datadog, Robert Marshall, Shopify, Zalando. No case names C#, Kotlin, PHP, Rust or Swift as the language it started from: lessons applied there are extrapolation.

- [Bloomberg opens 2,333 migration PRs for Python packaging and C++ builds with a hybrid pipeline](cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md) — mixed, an in-house shared-environment Python packaging model; CppBuild, an in-house C++ build system to PyPackaging, an in-house per-package dependency model; CMake; AI share: unstated; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. A rule-driven pipeline with Claude in bounded steps opened 2,333 packaging and build PRs; 729 were merged, and most got no decision from their owners.
- [Ping.gg ports the Go TypeScript 7 compiler to Rust with coding agents, after a restart](cases/2026-10-07-ping-tsgo-to-rust.md) — language, Go (TypeScript 7 native compiler, type checker, language server and API) to Rust (tsc-rs); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: over $420,000 in API-priced tokens in all (over $400,000 first attempts, ~$24,047 restart), self-estimates; the restart ran on flat-rate plans. A Go-to-Rust TypeScript compiler port stalled near 84% after over $400,000 in tokens; a restart reports parity on upstream tests, with known gaps; unaudited.
- [GitHub moves its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript to Rust using agents](cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) — language, TypeScript on Node.js and V8 to Rust (native library with a C ABI); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$120,000 for ~136.3 billion tokens (engineer time not priced). One engineer steered agent fleets to port about 430,000 lines of TypeScript to Rust in place, one component per PR, over 14.5 weeks.
- [Shopify rebuilds its React Native mobile apps natively for iOS and Android](cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md) — language, React Native apps (Shop first; Shopify, Point of Sale, Inbox to follow) to native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI) and Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) apps; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents port Shopify's React Native apps to native iOS and Android in gated checkpoints; the author says one-shot ports fail. The Shop app shipped in 12 weeks.
- [Temporal moves its Cloud billing store to ClickHouse with coding agents doing most of the cleanup](cases/2026-09-02-temporal-billing-store-clickhouse.md) — data, previous data warehouse (not named) behind the usage and billing tables to ClickHouse (ClickHouse Cloud); AI share: part; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Saved agent prompts cover most deleted code and little new code; a shadow comparison caught an overflow, and agent instructions went stale.
- [Checkly rewrites its Node.js results daemon in Go with Claude Code](cases/2026-09-01-checkly-nodejs-to-go.md) — language, Node.js background worker in plain JavaScript (Results Daemon) to Go service; AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: the accepted agent run fit in one day's token allowance of a $200 plan; the discarded run and people's time are not costed. A black-box harness with golden files from the legacy daemon judged an overnight agent rewrite in Go; its simplified queue model broke retries.
- [Intel's IDEAS harness ports the libgit2 command-line client in C to safe Rust](cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) — language, C (libgit2 command-line client) to safe Rust (no unsafe code); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$0.55 per symbol for translation (total unstated), plus ~$6.5 for repair. An LLM harness turned 112K lines of C into safe Rust that compiled but crashed; 8 person-hours guiding an agent got git blame working.
- [Asana finishes its Enzyme to React Testing Library move with Codex agents in two weeks](cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (frontend React tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$11,000 model usage plus ~$1,000 infrastructure. Up to 4 Codex agents on a 5-sentence prompt removed Enzyme in about 1.5 weeks of engineering time for about $12K; stale docs and slow lint got in the way.
- [Bun moves its JavaScript runtime off Zig onto Rust with Claude agents in 11 days](cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) — language, Zig (Bun runtime, bundler, package manager, test runner) to Rust (about 100 crates); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$165,000 at API list prices for the tokens used before merge (690 million output tokens, 5.9 billion fresh input tokens, 72 billion cached input tokens). One engineer ran about 50 Claude Code workflows, up to 64 agents at once, to port 535K lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days; 19 known regressions, all fixed.
- [GitLab uses AI agents to move its application rate limiter onto a shared Ruby gem](cases/2026-07-08-gitlab-rate-limiting.md) — architecture, Gitlab::ApplicationRateLimiter in the GitLab monolith (a Rack-level limiter moves next) to a single implementation in the labkit-ruby gem; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents moved 121 rate-limit keys onto one gem; 17 keys slipped past the plan, and a divergence shadow mode had flagged reached users.
- [Mindstone folds 86 Go services into one TypeScript monolith with coding agents](cases/2026-07-06-mindstone-go-to-typescript.md) — mixed, 86 Go microservices (RPC, Kafka, ScyllaDB, Redis on Kubernetes) to a single TypeScript service running on Cloud Run (Hono, graphql-yoga, Node 24); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote 86 Go services as one TypeScript service in about 2 weeks, checked by tests run on both: the first suite chased coverage, asserting nothing.
- [Datadog moves Stream Router storage off FoundationDB onto PostgreSQL and DuckDB](cases/2026-06-23-datadog-foundationdb-to-postgres.md) — data, FoundationDB key-value store (write path) and RocksDB snapshots (read path) to relational schema on PostgreSQL (write path) and DuckDB snapshots (read path); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. People redesigned a key-value store as a relational schema; Claude and Cursor ported the storage methods one failing test at a time.
- [1Password uses AI agents to refactor its Go monolith and begin a service extraction](cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) — architecture, Go monolith (B5), database transactions opened with MustBegin (panics on failure) to separately owned services; transaction calls that return errors; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote over 3,000 panicking transaction calls from a tight spec, but stumbled on a service extraction's ordering and invariants.
- [Lutz Leonhardt starts moving 44 Angular form components in a Spartacus fork to Signal Forms](cases/2026-04-13-lutz-leonhardt-spartacus-signal-forms.md) — framework, Angular Reactive Forms (FormBuilder, Validators) to Angular Signal Forms through SignalFormControl, the interop first stage; AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Claude Code sub-agents in worktrees moved Angular forms to Signal Forms, 34 of 44 marked done; a review found untested successes and silent rule changes.
- [PagerDuty's product manager gets Rundeck's Grails 7 upgrade to 99.7% passing tests in 9 days](cases/2026-04-13-pagerduty-rundeck-grails-7.md) — framework, Rundeck on Grails 6 (Spring Boot 2.7, Spring Security 5, Hibernate 5, Groovy 3, Java 11, javax) to Rundeck on Grails 7 (Spring Boot 3.2, Spring Security 6, Hibernate 6, Groovy 4, Java 17, jakarta); AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: $200 in AI tools. A product manager with Claude Sonnet 4.5 in Cursor took Rundeck to Grails 7 in 9 days before engineer review; a Groovy 4 equals() change dropped the admin role.
- [Uber moves 75K test classes off JUnit 4 onto JUnit 5 with OpenRewrite; an AI attempt failed](cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md) — test-framework, Java tests on JUnit 4 in a Bazel monorepo to Java tests on JUnit 5 (Jupiter engine on the JUnit Platform); AI share: little; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Contrast case. Rule-based OpenRewrite recipes moved over 75,000 Java test classes onto JUnit 5; a generative-AI attempt failed and AI only helped debug.
- [Ladybird ports its JavaScript engine front end from C++ to Rust with Claude Code and Codex](cases/2026-02-23-ladybird-libjs-rust.md) — language, C++ (LibJS lexer, parser, AST, scope analysis and bytecode generator) to Rust (one crate linked into LibJS through a C interface); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. - [Christopher Chedeau moves the Pokémon Showdown battle engine off TypeScript onto Rust with Claude Code](cases/2026-01-25-vjeux-pokemon-showdown-rust.md) — language, Pokémon Showdown battle engine (TypeScript; the post calls it JavaScript) to Rust; AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. One engineer had Claude Code write about 100k lines of Rust in a month, checked against the original on millions of seeded battles; no Rust written by hand.
- [Spotify runs fleet-wide migrations with its Honk background coding agent](cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) — mixed, many (for example Java AutoValue classes, old Scio versions, deprecated datasets) to many (for example Java records, the newest Scio, new dataset versions); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. - [Robert Marshall moves his Gatsby blog to Next.js with Claude Code, after a failed first run](cases/2025-08-09-robert-marshall-gatsby-to-nextjs.md) — framework, Gatsby (blog fed by headless WordPress) to Next.js App Router; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. - [Google widens int32 IDs to int64 in 39 migrations with an LLM pipeline](cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) — data, int32 ID fields in protocol buffer schemas and the code using them (Java, C++, Dart and others) to int64 ID fields; AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. - [Airbnb moves 3.5K React test files off Enzyme onto React Testing Library](cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React component tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. - [Zalando moves partner apps from one in-house UI component library to another with GPT-4o](cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md) — framework, in-house UI component library (React) to another in-house UI component library (React); AI share: part; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: under $40 per repository in GPT-4o API fees (estimate).
